title: Rational ordinary-to-derived Hom comparison for a finite-projective summand
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $t\in A$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Write $D(R)$ for the derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $Q_t:D(R)\to D(R)[1/t]$ for its scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Fix a K-injective resolution $j:R[0]\to I$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For an $R$-module sheaf $F$ put $B(F)=\mathcal Hom_R(F,R)[0]$ and $T(F)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(F[0],I)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]; postcomposition with $j$ gives the chain map $c_F:B(F)\to T(F)$. Suppose that for some integer $m\geq0$ there are morphisms $i:Q_t(F[0])\to Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])$ and $p:Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])\to Q_t(F[0])$ with $pi=1$. Then $Q_t(c_F)$ is an isomorphism. Moreover $Q_t(B(F))$ is a direct summand of $Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])$. The comparison $c_F$ is natural under module maps, and this naturality extends $A[1/t]$-linearly to maps in the scalar localization of the degree-zero module subcategory.
